name: Minami-Senju
tagline: Tokyo in 17 minutes and Otemachi in 23 minutes. Served by 3 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000.
summary: The station is in Arakawa City, served by JR Joban Line, Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line and Tsukuba Express. Journey times to the main business districts are 23 minutes to Otemachi, 30 minutes to Shinjuku, 40 minutes to Shibuya and 31 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. The station stands 1.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 1.5 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 1.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0.7 m to 2.2 m, a difference of 1.5 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 9 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 20 clinics and 10 pharmacies. Facilities recorded as hospitals lie at 木村病院, about 933 m away and 台東病院, about 1308 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 3 lines serve the station: JR Joban Line, Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line and Tsukuba Express. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 1 line, Tokyo Metro runs 1 line and Tsukuba Express runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 78.

rentRange.note: One room ¥90,000 to ¥100,000, 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000, 1LDK ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

802 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Minami-Senju. One-room rents run about ¥8,000 higher.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 10 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Among the 23 wards' stations, comparatively many of the points around this one fall inside the projected inundation area for the largest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 3 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.noiseSources: 山谷通り runs 116 m away, so whether a flat faces it changes what you hear indoors.
